premise: Not a list of libraries one could adopt — anyone can write that and none of it is checkable. Each row below was imported to get its version and grepped for across src, tools, analyses and tests to see whether this project actually uses it. The interesting column is INSTALLED AND UNUSED: capability already paid for and not spent.
confession: This project declares numpy and pandas as its dependencies and runs on a machine carrying scipy, statsmodels, scikit-learn, NetworkX, Numba and PyTorch. Until tools/multiplicity.py every statistic here was hand-rolled from numpy while scipy sat installed — and the first thing scipy found, on its first run, was that the calibrated z fails a normality test whose mean and variance it passes.

libraries.name: NumPy
libraries.would: The array. Everything else is built on it.
libraries.note: Declared, used everywhere. Nothing to argue about.

libraries.name: pandas
libraries.would: Tabular joins and the CSV boundary between stages.
libraries.note: Declared and used. The atlas joins are pandas.

libraries.name: SciPy
libraries.would: Distributions, goodness-of-fit, sparse matrices, optimisation.
libraries.note: The one that stings. Every statistic in this repository was hand-rolled from numpy while scipy sat installed, in a project whose entire argument is statistical care. tools/multiplicity.py is the first file to import it, and the first thing it found was that the calibrated z fails a normality test its mean and variance pass.

libraries.name: statsmodels
libraries.would: Multiple-testing correction, regression, and the diagnostics that go with it.
libraries.note: Benjamini-Hochberg is four lines to write and the reason not to write it is that the four lines are where the off-by-one lives. Now used for the FDR layer.

libraries.name: scikit-learn
libraries.would: Dimensionality reduction, clustering, and the metrics for both.
libraries.note: Available and unused. It is the obvious tool for the cell-state rung, which is currently one expression value per cell type rather than a cell-by-gene matrix.

libraries.name: NetworkX
libraries.would: Graph construction, propagation, community detection, centrality.
libraries.note: Available and unused. The lupus graph is hand-built and its propagation is written by hand; random walk with restart and heat diffusion are both one call here.

libraries.name: scipy.sparse
libraries.would: CSR/CSC matrices and the sparse linear algebra the thesis is about.
libraries.note: The computational thesis in this project is about sparse workloads on biological topology, and no sparse matrix has been constructed yet. This is the gap between the second thesis and the repository, stated as an import.

libraries.name: Numba
libraries.would: JIT compilation of numeric loops, including parallel ones.
libraries.note: Available and unused. The null resampling is the only hot loop here and it is small enough not to need it — worth saying, because reaching for a JIT before measuring is how projects acquire complexity they cannot justify.

libraries.name: PyTorch
libraries.would: Tensors on the GPU; the substrate every structure and language model runs on.
libraries.note: Installed with CUDA and unused. It is the entry point to the structure rung — ESMFold and the protein language models run on it — and that rung is currently named and not built.

libraries.name: PyArrow
libraries.would: Columnar storage; Parquet instead of CSV at the stage boundary.
libraries.note: Declared as an optional extra. The stage boundary is CSV, which is fine at 17,916 rows and stops being fine at the single-cell rung.

libraries.name: SymPy
libraries.would: Symbolic algebra.
libraries.note: Available and unused, and likely to stay that way: nothing here needs a closed form.

libraries.name: joblib
libraries.would: Parallel map and on-disk memoisation.
libraries.note: Available and unused. The pipeline's staleness tracking does the caching job at a coarser grain, which is the right grain for stages that take minutes.

libraries.name: Matplotlib
libraries.would: Static figures for the manuscript.
libraries.note: Not installed, and deliberately so: figures are data files rendered by the web app, so there is no second implementation of a chart to disagree with the first.

libraries.name: AnnData
libraries.would: The standard container for single-cell matrices with per-cell and per-gene annotation.
libraries.note: Not installed. It is the format the cell rung would arrive in, and the reason that rung is 'partial' rather than 'built'.

libraries.name: Scanpy
libraries.would: The single-cell analysis stack built on AnnData.
libraries.note: Not installed. Named in the thesis, absent from the machine.

libraries.name: Squidpy
libraries.would: Spatial single-cell: neighbourhood graphs, spatial statistics.
libraries.note: Not installed. The tissue rung is the largest hole in the ladder and this is the library that would fill it.

libraries.name: Biopython
libraries.would: Sequence and structure file handling, alignment.
libraries.note: Not installed. It is the mundane plumbing under any structural work.

libraries.name: MDTraj
libraries.would: Trajectory analysis for molecular dynamics.
libraries.note: Not installed. The dynamics rung needs a sampling engine before it needs an analyser, so this is downstream of a decision not yet made.

libraries.name: OpenMM
libraries.would: GPU molecular dynamics.
libraries.note: Not installed. The rung is about the sampling bottleneck, and this is where that bottleneck would actually be met.

libraries.name: PyHPO
libraries.would: Semantic similarity over the Human Phenotype Ontology.
libraries.note: Not installed. The dossiers parse HPO by hand; phenotype-to-phenotype distance is the obvious next measurement and needs an ontology-aware library.

libraries.name: Hypothesis
libraries.would: Property-based testing: generate inputs rather than enumerate them.
libraries.note: Not installed. For a null-calibration library the properties almost write themselves — calibrating a constant column must not change a ranking — and that is a stronger test than any fixed example.

resources.name: DepMap CRISPR (Chronos)
resources.gives: Gene effect across ~1,178 cell lines: the perturbation screen this whole library was hardened against.

resources.name: Human Phenotype Ontology
resources.gives: Disease-to-phenotype annotations, inheritance modes, the vocabulary itself.
resources.note: Carries the inheritance measurement behind the non-gene tab.

resources.name: Orphanet
resources.gives: Prevalence records with type and geography, gene associations, ages of onset.
resources.licence: CC BY-ND 4.0 — no derivatives may be redistributed
resources.note: The licence is why derived material stays local and is described rather than shipped. It shaped the architecture.

resources.name: Human Protein Atlas, single-cell
resources.note: The cell axis. Per cell TYPE, not per cell.

resources.name: ClinicalTrials.gov API v2
resources.gives: What is being tried right now, by disease and by intervention.
resources.note: Queried live and cached so the artefact stays reproducible.

resources.name: BioGRID
resources.gives: Curated protein-protein interactions — the subgraph a Merlin propagation would run on.
resources.note: Named in the thesis as the concrete next step and not downloaded. The lupus graph is hand-built in its place.

resources.name: STRING
resources.gives: Scored functional associations, with the score decomposed by evidence type.
resources.note: Denser than BioGRID and needs a threshold, which is a judgement this project would have to state rather than inherit.

resources.name: Reactome
resources.note: The Hippo axis is currently a hand-written gene list; this would make it a citation.

resources.name: ClinVar
resources.gives: Variant-level clinical interpretation, with the review status attached.
resources.note: The genotype rung stops at genes. Variants are where the thesis actually starts.

resources.name: gnomAD
resources.gives: Population allele frequency, and per-gene constraint.
resources.note: Constraint is the cheapest evidence that a gene tolerates no loss, and it is one file away.

resources.name: AlphaFold DB
resources.gives: Predicted structures for essentially every human protein, with per-residue confidence.
resources.note: The structure rung would begin here rather than with a folding run, which is the difference between a download and a GPU budget.

resources.name: UniProt
resources.gives: Domains, sites, isoforms, and the residue numbering everything else keys on.
resources.note: Without it a residue position is a number with no meaning.

resources.name: MONDO
resources.gives: A disease ontology that merges OMIM, Orphanet and DECIPHER identifiers.
resources.note: Would replace the exact-name matching the dossiers currently do — which is the same fragility that put five wrong ORPHA codes on this site once already.
